title: PointPillars (nuScenes-pretrained) zero-shot on TruckScenes mini_val, full 80 samples, all six LiDARs merged in an upright virtual frame: mAP 0.1005 (best single channel 0.0555)
dataset: MAN TruckScenes v1.2-mini, mini_val split (2 scenes, 80 samples, official split via truckscenes.utils.splits)
sensor_configuration: Headline: all six LiDARs merged per sample into one upright virtual LiDAR matching nuScenes LIDAR_TOP (gravity z, x right / y forward, 1.84 m above the ground below the centroid of the mounts), each sweep through its own ego pose. Each of the six was also run separately. LIDAR_TOP_FRONT (roof, pitched ~56 deg) was the channel first used (see experiment-log/0024)
annotation_schema: TruckScenes 12-class detection taxonomy (eval/detection/README.md remap of the 27-class general taxonomy)
model: PointPillars (mmdetection3d 1.4.0), pointpillars_hv_secfpn_sbn-all_8xb4-2x_nus-3d, official nuScenes-pretrained checkpoint pointpillars_nus_20210826_225857-f19d00a3.pth (zero-shot, no fine-tuning or training on TruckScenes)
conditions: unknown: no weather/scenario filtering applied, mixed conditions across the split's 2 scenes

environment.hardware: AMD Ryzen 7 5700U with Radeon Graphics, no NVIDIA GPU, no CUDA path (CPU-only inference)
environment.python: 3.11.9, dedicated venv truckscenes-devkit/detection-env (same as EXP-0006/0019, reused as-is)

commands: (channel comparison and merged run: the first, second and last commands repeated with --channel LIDAR_LEFT, LIDAR_RIGHT, LIDAR_TOP_LEFT, LIDAR_TOP_RIGHT, LIDAR_REAR, and ALL)

metrics.name: mAP
metrics.scope: TruckScenes 12-class detection taxonomy, mini_val split, center-distance thresholds {0.5, 1, 2, 4}m averaged per detection config, all six LiDARs merged in the upright virtual frame; per-class AP car 0.406, motorcycle 0.337 (26 scored objects), traffic_cone 0.260, trailer 0.110, pedestrian 0.049, barrier 0.034, truck 0.009, others 0.000

measurements.scope: LIDAR_TOP_FRONT (the channel first used); merged ALL 0.1005; single channels: LIDAR_LEFT 0.0555, LIDAR_RIGHT 0.0466, LIDAR_TOP_LEFT 0.0125, LIDAR_TOP_RIGHT 0.0107, LIDAR_REAR 0.0057. See docs/evidence/pr63-channel-comparison/summary.json

measurements.scope: superseded; kept for the record. 596 boxes tilted 54.6-58.2 degrees in world frame; see docs/pr63-input-frame-review.md

notes: Extends EXP-0019 (record 0022) to all 80 mini_val samples on one LiDAR channel. The first run (27 Sep) fed native LIDAR_TOP_FRONT points, mounted pitched about 56.23 degrees, straight to an upright-box checkpoint and scored mAP 0.0000. The PR #63 review found every output box tilted 54.6-58.2 degrees against upright ground truth, so that score was not interpretable. Its claim that a class-agnostic nearest-match check ruled out a coordinate bug is withdrawn. The script now rectifies points into an upright virtual LiDAR matching the checkpoint's training frame and maps boxes back out through the same frame. Geometry is covered by tests/test_truckscenes_pointpillars_infer.py (CI-safe, numpy only). --input-frame native reproduced the audited historical file box for box (every field within 2e-6), so the old path is unchanged and the old files are kept as the historical run. The rectified run gives mAP 0.0067 (NDS 0.0807, not a validated metric here), the first nonzero LiDAR AP on TruckScenes in this project, but still far from useful detection. Only 23.9% of the scored ground truth contains any point from that channel, a downward-tilted blind-spot sensor. On 4 Oct every LiDAR was run separately through the same pipeline. The level side LiDARs, which reach about 70% of the scored objects, score highest: LIDAR_LEFT mAP 0.0555 (car AP 0.202) and LIDAR_RIGHT 0.0466 (car AP 0.239). The four channels reaching 23-43% score 0.0057-0.0125. Score tracks coverage, but mounting and beam pattern also differ between channels, so this is evidence rather than a controlled isolation of cause. Merging all six (each sweep through its own ego pose; a single-channel rerun reproduced its committed predictions exactly) reaches 94.9% of scored objects and mAP 0.1005, with car AP 0.406. Trucks have full coverage (392/392) yet AP 0.009, and trailers 407/408 with AP 0.110: for these classes the low score is recognition, not visibility, which points to the nuScenes checkpoint not recognising heavy trucks. The merge is geometric only: other road users' motion between sweeps and sensor intensity scales are not corrected. hours_spent is approximate: about 0.33 h for the first run, about 1 h for the rectification rework, about 0.5 h for the channel comparison and about 0.75 h for the merged run.
